field_name: Multi-hop knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) with subgraph/context supervision and LLM fine-tuning

categories.name: Multi-hop KGQA over knowledge graphs
categories.description: Answering questions requiring chaining of facts over a knowledge graph; the shared problem framing of all analyzed work.

categories.name: Subgraph-centric reasoning
categories.description: Methods that restrict reasoning to a retrieved/induced subgraph rather than the whole KG.

categories.name: Learned / trainable subgraph retrieval
categories.description: Training a retriever (often decoupled from the reasoner) to induce a question-relevant subgraph, then reasoning over it with an embedding-based model.

categories.name: Inference-time GraphRAG retrieval and triplet ordering
categories.description: Retrieving a subgraph at inference via KG queries/path finding, optionally merging and ordering triplets, and conditioning an LLM prompt; no training-signal change.

categories.name: Supervision-signal design for multi-hop training
categories.description: Methods whose primary contribution is how the training signal is constructed or augmented, rather than the inference architecture.

categories.name: Intermediate-step supervision
categories.description: Generating or learning supervision at intermediate reasoning steps (e.g., intermediate entity distributions) when only the final answer is labeled.

categories.name: Context-augmented triple supervision
categories.description: Attaching surrounding context (supporting triples from the same source passage, forming a context graph) to each target triple/path and fine-tuning an LLM under KG-grounded vs CG-grounded regimes. This is the idea's own category.

categories.name: Adaptive repair / data-cleaning loops
categories.description: Detecting unresolved one-hop failures with an LLM judge, generating targeted corrective examples, continually fine-tuning, and quarantining noisy triples before downstream training.

categories.name: RL-based KG reasoning and lower-hop RL transfer
categories.description: Reinforcement-learning optimization over KG paths or QA items, including RL on lower-hop items to improve generalization to deeper-hop queries.

categories.name: Architecture-centric relational reasoning
categories.description: Improving multi-hop QA mainly by architectural design (graph networks, syntactic-semantic augmentation) rather than by supervision or retrieval.

categories.name: Knowledge-context quantity in multimodal QA
categories.description: Supplying a variable (question-dependent) number of KG triples as model context in knowledge-based multimodal QA, with explicit findings about context quantity (precision vs distraction).

idea_position: The idea sits in the 'Context-augmented triple supervision' leaf under 'Supervision-signal design for multi-hop training', and additionally spans the sibling leaf 'Adaptive repair / data-cleaning loops' and the RL branch 'RL-based KG reasoning and lower-hop RL transfer'. Its closest neighbor, arxiv:2609.12230, occupies the same three leaves simultaneously with method and evaluation overlap ~1.0/0.9, making the idea's intended position already populated rather than adjacent to it; the subgraph-context framing it shares with 'Subgraph-centric reasoning' is where it connects to the broader field, and arxiv:2406.09994 supplies the only contextual-quantity evidence (from multimodal QA) that bears on the idea's context-volume assumption.
dominant_approaches: Retrieve-or-induce a question-relevant subgraph, then reason over it with an embedding model or an LLM prompt (arxiv:2202.13296, SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace).
Augment the model's input with KG triples or subgraph text (GraphRAG-style prompting) rather than changing the training objective (SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace, arxiv:2406.09994).

Augment the training signal when only final answers are available, e.g. intermediate entity supervision (arxiv:2101.03737) or passage-local context triples attached to each target triple (arxiv:2609.12230).
Iterative data-centric training loops: detect failures, generate corrective examples, refine; optionally followed by RL on easier items (arxiv:2609.12230).
Path-based RL over KGs for compositional reasoning (doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2023.110760, and the RL stage of arxiv:2609.12230).
Architectural graph/syntactic-semantic encoders for relational reasoning (DSSAGN doi:10.3390/electronics13081436).
common_assumptions: Multi-hop reasoning should be restricted to a retrieved or induced (sub)graph rather than the full KG (arxiv:2202.13296, SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace).
Adding relevant context or intermediate supervision improves multi-hop reasoning relative to isolated facts/final-answer-only feedback (arxiv:2609.12230, arxiv:2101.03737, arxiv:2406.09994).
WebQSP, CWQ and MetaQA are representative multi-hop KBQA benchmarks (arxiv:2202.13296, arxiv:2101.03737, SG-RAG MOT).
Answer accuracy / Hits@1 / Exact Match is the appropriate primary metric (all analyzed work).
Subgraph/context size must be bounded, since larger contexts trade answer coverage against noise (arxiv:2202.13296, arxiv:2406.09994).
Synthetically generated QA items with verification filters are adequate supervision and evaluation for domain KGQA (arxiv:2609.12230).
common_benchmarks: In-domain COVID-19 economic multi-hop query set (GraphTrace)
common_metrics: Answer coverage rate of retrieved subgraphs (arxiv:2202.13296)
Retrieval and generation metrics incl. directness (GraphTrace)

repeated_limitations.description: Context/subgraph size is a trade-off: too small excludes the answer, too large introduces noise that degrades QA (arxiv:2202.13296); supplying a fixed larger number of triples is worse than a dynamic, question-fitted number, and the work title explicitly frames excess context as distracting (arxiv:2406.09994). This directly qualifies the idea's assumption that same-passage context helps.

Retrieval/prompting methods (GraphRAG-style) perform no training, no supervision-design comparison, no data repair, and no RL, leaving the training-side questions open (SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace, arxiv:2202.13296).

Evaluation is domain-specific and/or synthetic rather than on established public benchmarks, limiting external validity (disease-specific KGs in arxiv:2609.12230; COVID-19 economic KG in GraphTrace; synthetic QA items per arxiv:2609.12230 Section 6).

Claims are unverifiable from the retrieved artifact: DSSAGN reports no datasets, baselines, metrics or numbers in its abstract, and the path-based adversarial RL record has neither abstract nor accessible full text.

The evaluation set is modified by the method being evaluated: adaptive repair removes/quarantines triples and refreshes the validation set, after which models reach 100% on the 'cleaned retained' one-hop set (arxiv:2609.12230), creating a selection/cleaning confound.

No public code or data release could be found for the closest and most complex method (arxiv:2609.12230) or for GraphMERT, whereas the simpler subgraph-retrieval and intermediate-supervision baselines do release code (arxiv:2202.13296, arxiv:2101.03737).

underexplored_combinations: Context-augmented LLM supervision evaluated on standard public benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA) instead of only synthetic domain MCQ — but note this requires text-grounded KGs with passage provenance that Freebase-based benchmarks lack.

Matched-token / matched-context-size controls that isolate passage localization from raw supervision volume, plus a context-size sweep to test the inverted-U (precision vs excess) in LLM KGQA supervision.
A component-wise decomposition (context vs repair vs RL) with an untouched, never-edited held-out test set and seed-level variance reporting.

Combining intermediate-step supervision (arxiv:2101.03737) with context-triple supervision (arxiv:2609.12230), which are alternative answers to the same missing-signal problem and have not been compared.
Applying the repair loop to retrieved/prompted context (GraphRAG pipelines: SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace) rather than only to KG-extraction triples.
Cross-corpus transfer of context-augmented supervision (train on one text corpus/KG, test on another) to test whether the mechanism is domain-general.

contradictions.description: The idea's H1/H4 assume more same-passage context is (at least weakly) beneficial, but retrieved work in adjacent settings reports the opposite direction at high context volume: arxiv:2406.09994 is framed as 'Precision Empowers, Excess Distracts' and shows dynamic (question-fitted) triples beat fixed larger amounts, while arxiv:2202.13296 shows larger subgraphs introduce noise and reduce QA Hits@1 even as answer coverage rises. SG-RAG MOT likewise finds merging helps 'up to some point'.

arxiv:2609.12230 claims the repair stage yields 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets, presenting this as a strengthened factual foundation; because the same loop quarantines triples and refreshes the validation set, this claim is in tension with the standard requirement that evaluation data be independent of the method — accuracy gains and evaluation-set editing are not separable as reported.

Two distinct remedies are offered for the same 'missing multi-hop supervision' problem without being compared: learned intermediate-step supervision for an embedding state machine (arxiv:2101.03737) versus passage-local context triples for LLM SFT (arxiv:2609.12230). Which added signal (intermediate reasoning distributions vs surrounding factual context) drives multi-hop gains is unresolved.
